clue.text: Steered straight for Spooner's warning sign

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade their first sounds

parts.note: right can mean straight, as in a right line or right angle

explanation.surface: A driver steered straight ahead toward the warning sign.
explanation.walkthrough: Say LED RIGHT with the opening L and R sounds traded and it becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light is a signal telling traffic to stop, and more widely any warning of danger.

clue.text: Dodgy tear in tissue

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a suspicious rip in a paper handkerchief.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tissue" suggests a paper hankie, but it is the biological sense: layers of cells.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is one kind of tissue.

clue.text: Back in outskirts of Derby, it's dull

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the second
outskirts are the edges, so take only the first and last letters of Derby

parts.note: first and last letters of Derby
the back of something is its rear

explanation.surface: A returning visitor finds the edge of Derby a dull place.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a city in the English Midlands; "Back" reads as returning, but it is the noun for the hind part.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gloomy and tedious, as in a dull, grey day.

clue.text: I start to gentrify small room in house

indicators.note: the start of gentrify is its first letter

parts.note: the loo is the lavatory, a small room

explanation.surface: I begin to smarten up the box room at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The loo is British slang for the toilet. 'house' is a verb in the surface but the noun for a dwelling here.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dwelling built from blocks of snow.

clue.text: Cleanliness of prominent inherited item remarked upon

indicators.note: something remarked upon is spoken, so the answer is how the phrase sounds

explanation.surface: Someone comments on the tidiness of a notable family heirloom.
explanation.walkthrough: "Inherited item" suggests an heirloom, but it is a gene, the unit of heredity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the practice of keeping clean to stay healthy.

clue.text: Some Tabasco used for northern stew

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the last three letters of Tabasco run into the first four of used

explanation.surface: A cook adds a dash of hot sauce to a hearty northern stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside taba-SCO USE-d. It is the lamb or beef stew of Liverpool, in the north of England, which gave Liverpudlians their nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional dish: Liverpool's stew of meat, potatoes and vegetables.

clue.text: Numbed nerve that might be pointed out on chart

definitions.text: that might be pointed out on chart

parts.note: front is cheek or nerve, as in 'had the front to ask'

explanation.surface: A doctor points out a deadened nerve on a medical chart.
explanation.walkthrough: The chart is a weather map, where this boundary is drawn as a line with pointed triangles along it, so it is literally pointed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: weather charts mark advancing cold air with a line of triangular points.

clue.text: Half of amount stopped: not well managed

indicators.note: half of means only three of the six letters of amount are used, the back half

explanation.surface: Payments are cut by half and the accounts were run badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' keeps UNT, the back half of AMOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untended has been neglected, left without care or attention.

clue.text: Desires uncapped income

indicators.note: without its cap, meaning its top letter; in a down answer the first letter is the top

parts.note: desires = yearnings; uncapped drops the first letter

explanation.surface: People want an income with no upper limit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Uncapped income" reads as salary with no ceiling, but uncapped acts on desires, losing its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the money someone is paid for work.

clue.text: Those people including old record in religious study

indicators.note: including means the people word holds the next pieces

explanation.surface: Those people keep an old record of religious study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts O and LOG inside THEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Theology is the academic discipline concerned with God and faith.

clue.text: Roofer behind time after second run

parts.note: cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A roofer arrives late, a second time running.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are not in clue order: 'after' puts S first, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific kind of roofer: one who lays slates.

clue.text: Small label for animal

explanation.surface: A little ear tag clipped on livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: "Animal" is a very broad definition, so the wordplay does all the work here.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a male deer is one animal among many.

clue.text: Most limited and now rarest supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple: bendily, so the letters flex into a new order

explanation.surface: A shop notes that the scarcest stock is now also in the shortest supply.
explanation.walkthrough: "Supply" looks like a noun about stock; it is SUPPLE + -LY, meaning pliably, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: most restricted in scope or width.

clue.text: Mushrooms enjoyable with good sushi ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of sushi

explanation.surface: Mushrooms are tasty with good sushi, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are fruiting bodies of members of the plural kingdom of moulds and toadstools.

clue.text: Man maybe in tennis lesson

indicators.note: the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: the last two letters of tennis and the first two of lesson

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps, taking a tennis lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: "Man" is not a person but the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so it stands for any island.

clue.text: Moves around important parts for computer user

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: things for a computer user

parts.note: to shift is to move things around
the key parts are the important ones

explanation.surface: Someone rearranges the vital components on behalf of a computer user.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as office rearranging, but the answer is the keyboard buttons a typist presses for capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: keyboard buttons that anyone typing on a computer uses.

clue.text: Nice breakfast for reliable fellow

definitions.meaning: dated slang for a decent chap

explanation.surface: A pleasant breakfast served to a dependable chap.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is dated British slang for a decent, trustworthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a literal tasty egg, and an idiom for a kind, dependable person.

clue.text: That woman in 3-D is like an angel

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second

explanation.surface: A woman seen in a 3-D film looks angelic.
explanation.walkthrough: "3-D" is not a cross-reference to another clue; it means three-dimensional.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: like a cherub, one of the orders of angels, sweet and round-faced.

clue.text: Is it a rum fancy for dessert?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether an elaborate rum dish counts as pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: This pudding is often soaked in rum or another spirit, which makes the question apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an Italian coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone pudding.

clue.text: Calling hospital, feeling unwell

explanation.surface: Someone phoning the hospital because they feel ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling reads as telephoning, but the sense is shouting out to someone, as when flagging a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shouting a greeting or summons to someone.

clue.text: Marsh lying around one desert

indicators.note: lying the other way round, so the word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A marsh sits beside a lone desert.
explanation.walkthrough: "Around" looks like a container signal, but it turns the marsh round rather than wrapping the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the great desert of Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Alongside wife, I principally trust husband

indicators.note: take the principal, meaning first, letter

explanation.surface: A spouse declares trust in her husband above all.
explanation.walkthrough: "Principally" reads as "mainly" in the surface, but it takes only the first letter of trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean in the company of, as in walking beside someone.

clue.text: Our group would shortly sound a bell for celebration

parts.note: to ding is to sound a bell

explanation.surface: Our group would soon ring a bell to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would shortly' is the 'd of we'd.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a marriage ceremony and the festivities that follow.

clue.text: Behave better in religious education class

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A pupil learns to behave in the RE lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain; a form is a British school year group or class.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to mend one's ways, as a former offender does.

clue.text: Compulsive fan did act strangely

indicators.note: the letters appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: An obsessive fan behaved oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complete little story, so "strangely" passes as description rather than instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose sense: beyond drug dependency, the word is used of anyone hooked on a hobby, such as a football fanatic.

clue.text: Cook in right oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: An instruction to cook something in the correct oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is the kiln used to dry hops for brewing, often in a cone-roofed oast house in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific way to cook: with dry heat in an oven.

clue.text: Cover plot, badly parsed

parts.note: a plot of garden ground for plants is a bed, as in flower bed

indicators.note: badly here means put together wrongly, so the letters of parsed are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher complains that a storyline was poorly analysed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' and 'parsed' suggest a story and grammar, but a plot here is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the decorative top layer laid over a bed, so it is a cover.

clue.text: Fruit cordial ultimately a greyish colour

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of cordial

explanation.surface: A fruit drink turns out to be a dull grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl names a pale bluish-grey shade like the lustre of an oyster's gem.

clue.text: Central heating fixture beginning to burn fuel engineer's jacket

indicators.note: the beginning of burn is its first letter
a jacket is the outside, so only the outer letters of engineer are kept

parts.note: the engineer, with 's as a possessive link

explanation.surface: A heating engineer's jacket catches fire from burning oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' keeps ER, the first and last letters of engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler heats water for radiators in a home heating system.

clue.text: European capital excitedly into pasta

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: excitedly suggests letters jumping about, so the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist in a European capital gets thrilled about Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word telling the capital where to go, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a kind of Italian pasta made in short ridged tubes.

clue.text: Picked up teams for voyage at sea

indicators.note: picked up as by a microphone or ear, so it is how the word sounds

explanation.surface: Crews are collected to go on a sea trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Crews fits the sea scene, but here it only supplies the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pleasure trip by ship.

clue.text: I get mail edited for specific restriction

indicators.note: edited text is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's post is censored to meet a particular rule.
explanation.walkthrough: "Edited" fits the surface about censored post, which hides that it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a rule barring people above or below a set number of years is one specific restriction.
